chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:
Seven things are forbidden from the sheep — the blood, the two testicles, the penis, the bladder, the glands, the spleen, and the gallbladder.

key_terms.الشَّاةُ: Sheep or goat; generic term for small livestock in Islamic dietary law
key_terms.الْخُصْيَتَانِ: The two testicles — dual form, among the forbidden reproductive organs
key_terms.حُرِّمَ: Is forbidden/prohibited (passive verb indicating divine or jurisprudential prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What parts of a sheep are forbidden to eat according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) enumerates seven specific parts of a slaughtered sheep that are forbidden to consume. This ruling reflects Islamic jurisprudence's detailed approach to dietary law (halal and haram), specifying organs prohibited due to their nature. The audience — Shia Muslims seeking practical guidance on food permissibility — would have understood this as a definitive Imami ruling applicable to all small livestock.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Seven things are Prohibited from the sheep – The blood, and the two testicles, and the penis, and the bladder, and the glands, and the spleen, and the gallbladder’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Durust from Ibrahim ibn ‘ Abd al-Hamid who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Seven things in sheep are unlawful for food. Of such things is blood, testicles, penis, bladder, glands, spleen and gallbladder.”’
